subject: ArgoPay onboarding: SDK warmstart, timeouts & rate-fence playbook
messages:

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@argopay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding kick — SDK questions before integration

Hi Samir — great follow-up. I put together a short, practical playbook below and attached a mutual action plan so procurement has a clear path. TL;DR: start with SDK warmstart + permissive rate-fence in staging, use client-side retries with exponential backoff + jitter, and enable prefix caching for high-cardinality reads.

Playbook (concise):
- Stage: sandbox traffic only. Warmstart: run a 24-hour synthetic job that primes model KV caches (small, repeated requests mimicking production distributions).
- Client SDK config: safety first — 3 retries, base backoff 200ms, max backoff 2s, full-jitter. Per-request timeout = 10s for non-streaming; streaming endpoints use 60s connection keepalive and token-level idle timeout 5s.
- Rate fences: set per-route soft limits in staging (QPS) and a stricter hard limit in prod for throttling. Example for payouts: 
  - Validation API (fast, idempotent): soft 200 QPS, hard 400 QPS (burstable to 600 for 30s).
  - Transfer execute (stateful): soft 20 QPS, hard 50 QPS. Keep transfer paths single-threaded per-account where possible.
- Endpoint migration: point staging SDK config to the sandbox hostname first; use a single toggle in config (REDWOOD_API_HOST) to flip to prod endpoint once smoke tests pass.
- Observability: tag all requests with route, client_version, and attempt_id. Surface 95th pct latency and error budget burn per route in the Console.

Sample SDK snippet (Node) — initialize + retries + timeout (for your eng team):

const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY,
  host: process.env.REDWOOD_API_HOST || 'https://sandbox.redwood.ai',
  retry: {
    retries: 3,
    factor: 2,
    minTimeout: 200,
    maxTimeout: 2000,
    jitter: true
  },
  timeout: 10000
});

// call with route-level metadata
await client.generate({route: 'payouts/validation', input: payload, metadata: {client_version: 'argo-1.0.0'}})

Notes on caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repetitive preflight checks. Works best when keys are deterministic and TTL is tuned to business freshness (e.g., 30s for balance checks).

I'll attach the mutual-action-plan.xlsx so your procurement has the milestones. Monica — can you confirm SLA/credit language we should expect on the M A P? Vivek — can you add your recommended runtime kernel/quantization hint for the transfer route (low-latency, high-accuracy tradeoff).

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks — happy to take this into a short working session.

— Vanessa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Quick infra notes for Samir: 
- Warmstart resource: yes, we'll reserve a small dedicated warm pool for the 48–72 hour warmstart job; no SLA charge for the first 72 hours. Coordinate start window with your SRE (we need a 2-hour maintenance window to seed KV caches).
- Kernel hint: for validation route, recommend fp16 quantized model with a fast-attention kernel; for the transfer execute route, keep fp32 or 8-bit quantization with conservative sampling to avoid hallucinations.
- Rate fence enforcement: Redwood Console supports per-route soft/hard limits; we can provision default 5% headroom in staging.

Samir — are you OK with an infra prep window on Tuesday 11/10 at 02:00–04:00 PT to run the warmstart job?

— Vivek
Principal Engineer, Runtime

Thanks all — that all looks good. Confirmed the Tuesday 11/10 02:00–04:00 PT window with our SRE. Two follow-ups: 

1) We accepted the MAP and returned a signed copy to procurement (attached see stub).
2) Minor ask on SDK snippet: can you include a small retry-hook that marks non-idempotent calls (transfer execute) as non-retriable on 409/422? Our legal ops are nervous about accidental double-exec.

If you can drop that small code sample, we can start the warmstart run immediately after the prep window. Appreciate the fast turn.

— Samir
